description: Competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our team NASA Space Operation has developed an educational space project to inspire universe exploration. Led by Sami who coordinates the workflow, the team features Esha on game development, Shihab as UI/UX Designer, and Bayezid on project presentation. Fahmida and Rusafi drives educational research
summary:
SpaceSkribble is a free, real-time multiplayer drawing and guessing game that turns space education into play. Players join a room, take turns sketching planets, spacecraft, astronauts and other space concepts, and race to guess what others are drawing. It runs in any browser, so no download or special device is needed.

The game addresses our chosen challenge by making real NASA data approachable. Word prompts, images and "Did you know?" facts come from NASA sources such as APOD and the NASA Image and Video Library, so every round teaches something true about space. An AI assistant, NOVA, gives hints to help beginners, and Bangla mode and classroom mode make it usable for students and teachers in our region.

It matters because many students find space science distant or intimidating. By combining creativity, friendly competition and authentic NASA data, SpaceSkribble builds curiosity and vocabulary in a fun, social way that can reach learners worldwide.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

SpaceSkribble is a browser-based, real-time multiplayer drawing and guessing game with a space theme. Players register or log in, create or join a room, and take turns as the drawer. The drawer gets a space-related word (a planet, a rover, a constellation, an astronaut) and sketches it on a shared canvas. Everyone else guesses in chat, and points are awarded for fast, correct guesses. Drawing strokes are synced live between players, so the game feels instant.

REAL NASA DATA

Word prompts, images and short "Did you know?" facts are drawn from NASA resources including the APOD API, the NASA Image and Video Library and the NASA Exoplanet Archive. After each round, players see a real NASA fact about the word, so the game teaches while it entertains. An AI assistant called NOVA offers hints and explanations when players are stuck.

BENEFITS

- Makes space science fun and approachable for students and beginners

- Needs only a browser, so it works on low-cost phones and laptops

- Bangla mode and classroom mode let teachers and students in Bangladesh use it for lessons and group activities

- Encourages creativity, vocabulary building and teamwork

INTENDED IMPACT

We want learners to build curiosity about space through play. A teacher can run a classroom round on the solar system, and friends anywhere in the world can learn real NASA facts together.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

- Front end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas for drawing

- Real-time multiplayer: Socket.IO (or Firebase)

- Data: NASA Open APIs

- Design: Figma and Google Stitch for UI concepts

- Hosting: Netlify; code on GitHub

- AI assistance: listed in the "Use of AI" section

CREATIVITY

SpaceSkribble combines the familiar draw-and-guess format with authentic NASA content, so each game round doubles as a mini science lesson. Local-language support and a classroom mode make it more inclusive than a typical party game.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Accessibility: runs in any browser with no installation

- Safety: fixed space-themed word lists and moderated chat

- Performance: lightweight canvas drawing that works on slow connections

- Education: facts based on real NASA sources, not made-up content

- Inclusion: Bangla language support and a free-to-play model
